# Packages installed into the managed venv, on top of a CUDA-matched PyTorch.
#
# torch and torchvision are NOT listed here: their version floor depends on the
# CUDA backend chosen for this machine, and the line is generated by
# ``bootstrap/venv_manager.py`` so that the requirements text and the index URL
# can never disagree.
#
# Ultralytics is deliberately unpinned, so a fresh environment gets the newest
# release. An existing environment moves forward only through Step 1's update
# button, which shows the resolution plan before changing anything. The cost is
# that a release can change behaviour underneath the app -- the 8.4 line renamed
# export arguments mid-series (``half``/``int8`` became ``quantize``) -- so the
# app reads such details off the installed version rather than assuming them:
# Step 6 looks the precision keyword up in ``DEFAULT_CFG_DICT``.
ultralytics

# OWLv2 for Step 3. transformers 5 is a major release we have not tested.
#
# The floor is 4.52 because that is where the torchvision-backed image
# processors were rolled out and ``use_fast=True`` became the default. Step 3
# asks for that processor explicitly: it resizes on the GPU, where the older one
# does it on a single CPU core while the card waits. Measured on four photos,
# 5 ms against 349. An older transformers still works -- the command times the
# candidates and says which it got -- it is just several times slower.
transformers>=4.52,<5

# Not a mistake, and not transitively installed by anything above. OWLv2's image
# processor resizes with anti-aliasing implemented over ``scipy.ndimage``, and
# transformers declares scipy as an optional backend -- so autolabeling fails at
# the first photo with "requires the scipy library" unless it is asked for here.
# Ultralytics used to pull it in and no longer does.
scipy>=1.11

# INT8 quantisation-aware training, for Step 5's QAT toggle. Ultralytics drives
# QAT itself (``train(quantize=8)``), but this is what it uses to insert the
# fake-quantisation, calibrate it and fine-tune with 8-bit rounding in the loop.
#
# Pinned exactly, for a sharper version of the reason Ultralytics is. The wheel
# itself is harmless -- 2 MB of pure Python, which compiles its CUDA kernels
# with ninja at first use rather than at install time -- but it carries a floor
# on torch, currently >=2.8. A release that raised that floor past the newest
# torch on an older CUDA index would fail the *whole* environment build, for
# every user, including the ones who will never tick the QAT box. So it moves
# only after someone has checked that its torch floor is still reachable on
# every index in planner.BACKENDS -- planner.newest_torch() against each
# backend's own index answers that in one page fetch per backend. At 0.46.1 the
# floor is torch>=2.8 and the tightest backend, cu128, carries 2.11.
#
# It is deliberately in OPTIONAL_PACKAGES rather than REQUIRED_PACKAGES: if it
# is missing or will not import, only the QAT toggle stops working, and locking
# Steps 2-7 behind it would be a worse bug than the one that reports.
nvidia-modelopt==0.46.1

# Export and Step 7 inference. Pre-installed rather than left to Ultralytics'
# on-demand ``check_requirements``, which would pip-install into the venv
# mid-export -- slow, surprising, and impossible behind a strict proxy.
onnx>=1.16
onnxslim>=0.1.48
onnxruntime-gpu>=1.19; platform_machine == "x86_64"
onnxruntime>=1.19; platform_machine != "x86_64"
# Already a dependency of nvidia-modelopt, and listed anyway because the app
# depends on it more specifically than modelopt does: not on the module being
# importable, but on the *executable* pip drops in the environment's script
# directory. torch.utils.cpp_extension decides whether it can build modelopt's
# INT8 kernels by running "ninja --version", so the app has to put that
# directory on the worker's PATH -- see worker_env._with_scripts_dir, which is
# the fix for exactly this. Pinned because it is a build tool whose output is
# cached across runs.
ninja==1.13.2

# Step 6's TensorRT format. It is the one export that is a compilation rather
# than a graph rewrite -- the engine is built for the card in the machine --
# and it is here for the same reason onnx is, except more so: this one is
# roughly 2 GB, and having Ultralytics fetch it in the middle of an export is
# the worst moment to discover that.
#
# Deliberately unpinned for now, and that is worth a second look. The
# ``tensorrt`` metapackage tracks one CUDA major at a time: at 11.3.0.99 it
# resolves to ``tensorrt_cu13``, so an environment built on the cu126 or cu128
# backend ends up with a CUDA 13 TensorRT beside a CUDA 12 torch. The wheels
# carry their own runtime libraries, so this works -- at the cost of a second
# copy of one. Choosing ``tensorrt-cu12`` or ``tensorrt-cu13`` to match the
# backend is the tidier answer, and it belongs with the generated torch line in
# ``bootstrap/venv_manager.py`` rather than in this file, which cannot see
# which backend was picked.
tensorrt

# Part of nvidia-modelopt's "onnx" extra, written out a line at a time rather
# than as ``nvidia-modelopt[onnx]``, so that each one shows up in the plan Step 1
# displays before it installs anything. Together they are what makes
# ``modelopt.onnx`` usable, which is the path a TensorRT export takes in Step 6:
# INT8 goes through ``modelopt.onnx.quantization``, FP16 through
# ``modelopt.onnx.autocast``. The app imports none of these itself.
#
# Ultralytics will not fetch them for us. Its export calls
# ``check_requirements("nvidia-modelopt[onnx]>=0.44")``, but that check ignores
# the extra and only asks whether nvidia-modelopt is installed -- which it is,
# from the line above -- so a missing one surfaces as an ImportError partway
# through the export.
#
# Unpinned because modelopt is pinned, and the pin above is what stops the
# extra changing underneath the app. At 0.46.1 the extra is larger than this
# list: onnx, onnxslim and onnxruntime are covered above, ml_dtypes arrives as
# a dependency of onnx, and cppimport, cupy-cuda12x and onnxconverter-common are
# not installed. If an export ever fails on a missing module, those three are
# the first place to look.
onnx_graphsurgeon   # the graph rewriter
onnxscript          # what torch's newer ONNX exporter builds a graph with
lief                # modelopt's own executable-format reader
polygraphy          # imported by modelopt.onnx.autocast, i.e. every FP16 TensorRT export
